functions.name: graphRoute
functions.description: Finds a route through an integer-id graph. Edges may be `{from,to}`, `{a,b}`, `{province_a,province_b}`, or `{from_id,to_id}` arrays. Options: `directed`, `algorithm` ("bfs"|"dijkstra"), and optional `cost(from, to)`.
functions.params_doc:
- `edges` â€” `table`: Array of graph edge tables.
- `from` â€” `integer`: Start node id.
- `to` â€” `integer`: Target node id.
- `opts` â€” `table?`: Options with `directed`, `algorithm`, and `cost` callback; a function may be passed directly as the cost callback.
typed_params: Options with `directed`, `algorithm`, and `cost` callback; a function may be passed directly as the cost callback.
functions.return_description: Node id route from start to target, or nil when unreachable.

functions.name: graphRoutes
functions.description: Finds routes for a batch of graph `{from, to}` requests using the same edge table and options as `graphRoute`.
functions.params_doc:
- `edges` â€” `table`: Array of graph edge tables.
- `requests` â€” `table`: Array of `{from=integer,to=integer}` or `{from,to}` route requests.
- `opts` â€” `table?`: Options with `directed`, `algorithm`, and `cost` callback; a function may be passed directly as the cost callback.
typed_params: Options with `directed`, `algorithm`, and `cost` callback; a function may be passed directly as the cost callback.
functions.return_description: Array of route arrays; unreachable entries are nil.

functions.name: graphConnectedComponents
functions.description: Returns connected components for an integer-id graph. Pass `nodes` to include isolated node ids.
functions.params_doc:
- `edges` â€” `table`: Array of graph edge tables.
- `nodes` â€” `table?`: Optional array of node ids; omitted nodes are inferred from edge endpoints.
- `opts` â€” `table?`: Options with `directed`; directed graphs follow outgoing edges.
typed_params: Optional array of node ids; omitted nodes are inferred from edge endpoints.
Options with `directed`; directed graphs follow outgoing edges.
functions.return_description: Array of node-id arrays, sorted by first node id.

functions.name: graphConnected

functions.params_doc:

- `to` â€” `integer`: Target node id.
- `opts` â€” `table?`: Options with `directed`.

LProvinceRegistry.description: Handle to a named province registry, exposing spatial queries, style mutations, rendering, and change tracking to Lua scripts.

methods.name: getName

methods.full_doc:
Returns the string name used to identify this registry in the province system.
@return | string | The registry name passed to `newFromPng`.

functions.name: push
functions.description: Push a new scene onto the stack, making it the active scene. The previously-active scene receives its `pause()` lifecycle callback and the new scene receives `enter(self, params)`. An optional visual transition (fade, slide, iris, etc.) animates between the two scenes over the specified duration.
functions.params_doc:
- `scene` â€” `table`: A scene table with lifecycle methods (`enter`, `leave`, `pause`, `resume`, `update`, `draw`, etc.).
- `transition` â€” `string?`: Transition type name: `"fade"`, `"slideleft"`, `"slideright"`, `"slideup"`, `"slidedown"`, `"wipe"`, `"iris"`, `"zoom"`, `"crossfade"`. Defaults to `"none"`.
- `duration` â€” `number?`: Transition animation duration in seconds. Defaults to 0 (instant).
- `easing` â€” `string?`: Easing curve name (e.g. `"linear"`, `"ease_in"`, `"ease_out"`, `"ease_in_out"`). Defaults to `"linear"`.
- `params` â€” `table?`: Arbitrary data forwarded to the new scene's `enter(self, params)` callback for initialization.
typed_params: A scene table with lifecycle methods (`enter`, `leave`, `pause`, `resume`, `update`, `draw`, etc.).
Transition animation duration in seconds. Defaults to 0 (instant).
Arbitrary data forwarded to the new scene's `enter(self, params)` callback for initialization.

functions.name: pop
functions.description: Pop the top scene off the stack and return to the previous one. The popped scene receives `leave()` and the revealed scene receives `resume()` (unless the popped scene was an overlay, in which case the underlying scene was never paused). Use this for "back" navigation, closing menus, or exiting sub-screens.
functions.params_doc:
- `transition` â€” `string?`: Transition type name. Defaults to `"none"` (instant).
- `duration` â€” `number?`: Transition animation duration in seconds. Defaults to 0.
- `easing` â€” `string?`: Easing curve name. Defaults to `"linear"`.
typed_params: Transition animation duration in seconds. Defaults to 0.

functions.name: switchTo
functions.description: Replace the current top scene with a different one without changing stack depth. The old scene receives `leave()` and the new scene receives `enter(self, params)`. Unlike `push`, no scene is added to the stack â€” the old scene is removed and the new one takes its slot. Ideal for transitioning between peer-level game states (e.g. level 1 â†’ level 2).
functions.params_doc:
- `scene` â€” `table`: The replacement scene table.
- `transition` â€” `string?`: Transition type name. Defaults to `"none"`.
- `duration` â€” `number?`: Transition animation duration in seconds. Defaults to 0.
- `easing` â€” `string?`: Easing curve name. Defaults to `"linear"`.
- `params` â€” `table?`: Arbitrary data forwarded to the new scene's `enter(self, params)` callback.
typed_params: Transition animation duration in seconds. Defaults to 0.
Arbitrary data forwarded to the new scene's `enter(self, params)` callback.

functions.name: clear
functions.description: Remove all scenes from the stack. Each removed scene receives its `leave()` callback in stack order. After this call the stack is empty and `isEmpty()` returns true. Useful for returning to a title screen or tearing down the entire scene graph.
functions.full_doc: Remove all scenes from the stack. Each removed scene receives its `leave()` callback in stack order. After this call the stack is empty and `isEmpty()` returns true. Useful for returning to a title screen or tearing down the entire scene graph.

functions.name: popTo
functions.description: Pop scenes off the stack until the named registered scene is on top. Every popped scene receives `leave()` and the target scene receives `resume()`. The target scene must have been previously added via `registerScene`. Returns false if no scene with that name exists on the stack.
functions.params_doc: - `name` â€” `string`: The registered name of the target scene to unwind to.
typed_params: The registered name of the target scene to unwind to.
functions.return_description: True if the named scene was found and is now the active top scene, false if the name was not found.

functions.name: update
functions.description: Advance any active transition animation and call `update(self, dt)` on the current top scene.
functions.params_doc: - `dt` â€” `number`: Delta time in seconds since the last frame (e.g. from `lurek.timer.getDelta()`).
typed_params: Delta time in seconds since the last frame (e.g. from `lurek.timer.getDelta()`).

functions.name: process
functions.description: Call `ready(self)` once on newly-pushed scenes, then call `process(self, dt)` on every process-active scene ordered by layer (lowest first).
functions.params_doc: - `dt` â€” `number`: Fixed time-step delta in seconds (e.g. 1/60 for 60-tick logic).
typed_params: Fixed time-step delta in seconds (e.g. 1/60 for 60-tick logic).

functions.name: processPhysics
functions.description: Call `process_physics(self, dt)` on every process-active scene ordered by layer.
functions.params_doc: - `dt` â€” `number`: Physics time-step delta in seconds.

functions.name: processLate

functions.params_doc: - `dt` â€” `number`: Delta time in seconds (same value passed to `process`).
typed_params: Delta time in seconds (same value passed to `process`).

functions.name: draw
functions.description: Call `draw(self)` on render-active scenes ordered by layer (lowest first).
functions.full_doc:
Call `draw(self)` on render-active scenes ordered by layer (lowest first).
Engine-level render policy is single-scene: only the current top scene is rendered.
This is the legacy draw callback â€” prefer `render` and `renderUi` for world-space and screen-space separation.

functions.name: render
functions.description: Call `render(self)` on render-active scenes ordered by layer (lowest first).
functions.full_doc:
Call `render(self)` on render-active scenes ordered by layer (lowest first).
Engine-level render policy is single-scene: only the current top scene is rendered.
This is the preferred world-space rendering callback â€” draw sprites, tilemaps, particles, and other in-world visuals here. Runs before `renderUi`.

functions.name: renderUi

functions.full_doc:
Call `render_ui(self)` on render-active scenes ordered by layer (lowest first).
Engine-level render policy is single-scene: only the current top scene is rendered.
Use this for screen-space HUD elements, health bars, score displays, menus, and overlays that should draw on top of the world after `render`.

LDepthSorter.description: Depth sorter exposed to Lua as `LDepthSorter`. Collects draw callbacks or drawable objects with numeric depth values and flushes them in back-to-front order for correct painter's-algorithm rendering. Ideal for sorting sprites, particles, and layered game objects within a single scene.

methods.name: add
methods.description: Register a draw callback at a given depth value. When `flush` is called, all registered callbacks execute in back-to-front order (lowest depth drawn first, highest depth drawn last / on top). Use this for simple draw calls like sprite rendering where each entity has a depth/z-layer.
methods.params_doc:
- `callback` â€” `function`: A zero-argument draw function invoked during flush.
- `depth` â€” `number`: Numeric z-depth controlling draw order â€” lower values are drawn behind higher values.
typed_params: A zero-argument draw function invoked during flush.

methods.description: Register a game object table for depth-sorted rendering. The object must expose a numeric `depth` field and a `drawSorted(self)` method. During `flush`, each object's `drawSorted` is called in depth order, making this ideal for entity-based architectures where objects manage their own drawing.
methods.full_doc:
Register a game object table for depth-sorted rendering. The object must expose a numeric `depth` field and a `drawSorted(self)` method. During `flush`, each object's `drawSorted` is called in depth order, making this ideal for entity-based architectures where objects manage their own drawing.
@param | obj | table | A game object table with a numeric `depth` field and a `drawSorted(self)` method.
methods.params_doc: - `obj` â€” `table`: A game object table with a numeric `depth` field and a `drawSorted(self)` method.
typed_params: A game object table with a numeric `depth` field and a `drawSorted(self)` method.

methods.description: Sort all registered entries by depth without executing any callbacks. Call this only if you need to inspect the sorted order before drawing; `flush` already sorts automatically.
methods.full_doc: Sort all registered entries by depth without executing any callbacks. Call this only if you need to inspect the sorted order before drawing; `flush` already sorts automatically.

methods.name: flush
methods.description: Sort all entries by depth, execute every callback or object's `drawSorted` method in back-to-front order, then clear the sorter for the next frame. This is the standard one-call render path â€” call it once per frame inside your scene's `draw` or `render` callback.
methods.full_doc: Sort all entries by depth, execute every callback or object's `drawSorted` method in back-to-front order, then clear the sorter for the next frame. This is the standard one-call render path â€” call it once per frame inside your scene's `draw` or `render` callback.

@return | integer | Total frame count.

functions.name: step
functions.description: Advances the internal clock by one tick and returns the delta time for that tick. Typically called by the engine loop; game scripts rarely need this.
functions.full_doc:
Advances the internal clock by one tick and returns the delta time for that tick. Typically called by the engine loop; game scripts rarely need this.
@return | number | Delta time in seconds for the step.
functions.return_description: Delta time in seconds for the step.

functions.name: getMicroTime
functions.description: Returns high-resolution elapsed time in seconds since engine start. Useful for precise benchmarking and profiling.
functions.full_doc:
Returns high-resolution elapsed time in seconds since engine start. Useful for precise benchmarking and profiling.
@return | number | Elapsed time in seconds with sub-microsecond precision.
functions.return_description: Elapsed time in seconds with sub-microsecond precision.

functions.name: getPhysicsDelta
functions.description: Returns the fixed timestep used for physics simulation in seconds. The default is typically 1/60.
functions.full_doc:
Returns the fixed timestep used for physics simulation in seconds. The default is typically 1/60.
@return | number | Fixed physics delta time in seconds.
functions.return_description: Fixed physics delta time in seconds.

functions.name: setPhysicsDelta
functions.description: Sets the fixed timestep for physics simulation. Clamped between 1/240 and 1/10 seconds. Lower values increase accuracy but cost more CPU.
functions.full_doc:
Sets the fixed timestep for physics simulation. Clamped between 1/240 and 1/10 seconds. Lower values increase accuracy but cost more CPU.
@param | dt | number | Desired fixed delta time in seconds.
functions.params_doc: - `dt` â€” `number`: Desired fixed delta time in seconds.
typed_params: Desired fixed delta time in seconds.

functions.name: getPhysicsMaxSteps
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of physics steps allowed per frame. Prevents the spiral of death when the game runs slowly.
functions.full_doc:
Returns the maximum number of physics steps allowed per frame. Prevents the spiral of death when the game runs slowly.
@return | number | Maximum physics steps per frame.

functions.name: setPhysicsMaxSteps
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of physics steps allowed per frame. Clamped between 1 and 64. Higher values improve accuracy under lag but cost more CPU.
functions.full_doc:
Sets the maximum number of physics steps allowed per frame. Clamped between 1 and 64. Higher values improve accuracy under lag but cost more CPU.
@param | n | integer | Maximum physics steps per frame.
functions.params_doc: - `n` â€” `integer`: Maximum physics steps per frame.

functions.name: sleep
functions.description: Blocks the current thread for the given number of seconds. Use sparingly â€” this halts the entire game loop. Intended for loading screens or synchronization.
functions.full_doc:
Blocks the current thread for the given number of seconds. Use sparingly â€” this halts the entire game loop. Intended for loading screens or synchronization.
@param | seconds | number | Duration to sleep in seconds.
functions.params_doc: - `seconds` â€” `number`: Duration to sleep in seconds.

functions.name: newScheduler
functions.description: Creates a new LScheduler instance for managing timed and frame-based callbacks independently from the global timer. Each scheduler has its own time scale and event list.
functions.full_doc:
Creates a new LScheduler instance for managing timed and frame-based callbacks independently from the global timer. Each scheduler has its own time scale and event list.
@return | LScheduler | A new scheduler object.

functions.name: chain
functions.description: Creates a scheduler pre-loaded with a sequence of delayed callbacks. Each step is a table with an optional `delay` (seconds) and optional `func` (callback). Delays accumulate so each step fires after the sum of all preceding delays. Returns the scheduler for manual update calls.
functions.params_doc: - `steps` â€” `table`: Array of step tables, each with optional fields `delay` (number) and `func` (function).
typed_params: Array of step tables, each with optional fields `delay` (number) and `func` (function).
functions.return_description: A new scheduler pre-loaded with the chained events.

functions.name: afterReal
functions.description: Schedules a one-shot callback based on real (wall-clock) time, unaffected by game pausing or time scaling. Use for UI fade-outs, notifications, or anything that should run on real time.
functions.params_doc:
- `delay` â€” `number`: Real-time delay in seconds before the callback fires.
- `func` â€” `function`: Callback to invoke when the real-time deadline is reached.
typed_params: Real-time delay in seconds before the callback fires.
Callback to invoke when the real-time deadline is reached.

functions.name: tickRealTimers
functions.description: Checks all real-time timers and fires any whose deadline has passed. Returns the number of callbacks that fired. Call this once per frame after afterReal scheduling.
functions.full_doc:
Checks all real-time timers and fires any whose deadline has passed. Returns the number of callbacks that fired. Call this once per frame after afterReal scheduling.
@return | integer | Count of real-time callbacks that fired.
functions.return_description: Count of real-time callbacks that fired.

functions.name: setSmoothingFactor
functions.description: Sets the exponential smoothing factor used by getSmoothedDelta. Lower values produce smoother (more lagged) results; higher values track changes faster. Clamped to [0.01, 1.0].
functions.full_doc:
Sets the exponential smoothing factor used by getSmoothedDelta. Lower values produce smoother (more lagged) results; higher values track changes faster. Clamped to [0.01, 1.0].
@param | alpha | number | Smoothing factor between 0.01 and 1.0.
functions.params_doc: - `alpha` â€” `number`: Smoothing factor between 0.01 and 1.0.

functions.name: getSmoothedDelta
functions.description: Returns an exponentially smoothed delta time in seconds, reducing frame-to-frame jitter. Call once per frame for consistent results. The smoothing factor is set via setSmoothingFactor.
functions.full_doc:
Returns an exponentially smoothed delta time in seconds, reducing frame-to-frame jitter. Call once per frame for consistent results. The smoothing factor is set via setSmoothingFactor.
@return | number | Smoothed delta time in seconds.

functions.name: waitSeconds
functions.description: Yields the current coroutine for the given number of real-time seconds. Must be called from within a coroutine. The coroutine is resumed automatically when tickWaits is called and the deadline has passed.
functions.full_doc:
Yields the current coroutine for the given number of real-time seconds. Must be called from within a coroutine. The coroutine is resumed automatically when tickWaits is called and the deadline has passed.
@param | seconds | number | Real-time seconds to wait.
functions.params_doc: - `seconds` â€” `number`: Real-time seconds to wait.

functions.name: waitFrames
functions.description: Yields the current coroutine for the given number of frames. Must be called from within a coroutine. The coroutine is resumed automatically when tickWaits is called and the target frame count has been reached.
functions.full_doc:
Yields the current coroutine for the given number of frames. Must be called from within a coroutine. The coroutine is resumed automatically when tickWaits is called and the target frame count has been reached.
@param | frames | integer | Number of frames to wait.
functions.params_doc: - `frames` â€” `integer`: Number of frames to wait.

functions.name: tickWaits
functions.description: Checks all pending waitSeconds and waitFrames coroutines, resumes any whose deadline or frame target has been reached, and cleans up completed entries. Returns the number of coroutines that were resumed. Call once per frame.
functions.full_doc:
Checks all pending waitSeconds and waitFrames coroutines, resumes any whose deadline or frame target has been reached, and cleans up completed entries. Returns the number of coroutines that were resumed. Call once per frame.
@return | integer | Count of coroutines resumed.

LScheduler.description: A Lua-exposed event scheduler that fires callbacks after timed delays or frame counts, with support for repeating intervals, named entries, pausing, and time-scaling.

methods.name: after
methods.description: Schedules a one-shot callback to fire after the given delay in seconds. Returns an event ID that can be used to cancel, pause, or query the event.
methods.params_doc:
- `delay` â€” `number`: Time in seconds before the callback fires.
- `func` â€” `function`: Callback to invoke when the delay elapses.
typed_params: Time in seconds before the callback fires.
Callback to invoke when the delay elapses.
methods.return_description: Unique event ID for this scheduled callback.

methods.name: afterFrames
methods.description: Schedules a one-shot callback to fire after the given number of frames. Returns an event ID for management.
methods.params_doc:
- `n` â€” `integer`: Number of frames to wait before the callback fires.
- `func` â€” `function`: Callback to invoke when the frame count elapses.
typed_params: Number of frames to wait before the callback fires.
Callback to invoke when the frame count elapses.
methods.return_description: Unique event ID for this scheduled callback.

methods.name: afterNamed

typed_params: Unique name for this scheduled event.
Time in seconds before the callback fires.
Callback to invoke when the delay elapses.
methods.return_description: Unique event ID for this scheduled callback.

methods.description: Schedules a repeating callback that fires at a fixed interval in seconds. Pass a positive count to limit repetitions, or omit/pass -1 to repeat indefinitely.
methods.params_doc:
- `interval` â€” `number`: Time in seconds between each invocation.
- `func` â€” `function`: Callback to invoke on each interval tick.
- `count` â€” `integer?`: Maximum number of times to fire. Defaults to -1 (infinite).
typed_params: Time in seconds between each invocation.
Callback to invoke on each interval tick.
Maximum number of times to fire. Defaults to -1 (infinite).
methods.return_description: Unique event ID for this repeating callback.

methods.name: everyFrames
methods.description: Schedules a repeating callback that fires every N frames. Pass a positive count to limit repetitions, or omit/pass -1 to repeat indefinitely.
methods.params_doc:
- `n` â€” `integer`: Number of frames between each invocation.
- `func` â€” `function`: Callback to invoke on each frame-interval tick.
- `count` â€” `integer?`: Maximum number of times to fire. Defaults to -1 (infinite).
typed_params: Number of frames between each invocation.
Callback to invoke on each frame-interval tick.
Maximum number of times to fire. Defaults to -1 (infinite).
methods.return_description: Unique event ID for this repeating callback.

methods.name: everyNamed
methods.description: Schedules a named repeating callback at a fixed interval. If a callback with the same name already exists, the old one is cancelled and replaced. Useful for restartable periodic effects like health regeneration or status ticks.
methods.params_doc:
- `name` â€” `string`: Unique name for this repeating event.
- `interval` â€” `number`: Time in seconds between each invocation.
- `func` â€” `function`: Callback to invoke on each interval tick.
- `count` â€” `integer?`: Maximum number of times to fire. Defaults to -1 (infinite).
typed_params: Unique name for this repeating event.
Time in seconds between each invocation.
Callback to invoke on each interval tick.
Maximum number of times to fire. Defaults to -1 (infinite).
methods.return_description: Unique event ID for this repeating callback.

methods.name: cancel
methods.description: Cancels a scheduled event by its ID. Returns true if the event was found and removed, false if it did not exist.
methods.params_doc: - `id` â€” `integer`: Event ID returned by after, every, or their variants.
typed_params: Event ID returned by after, every, or their variants.
methods.return_description: True if the event was found and cancelled.

methods.name: cancelNamed
methods.description: Cancels a named scheduled event. Returns true if the named event was found and removed.
methods.params_doc: - `name` â€” `string`: The name used when scheduling with afterNamed or everyNamed.
typed_params: The name used when scheduling with afterNamed or everyNamed.
methods.return_description: True if the named event was found and cancelled.

methods.name: cancelAll
methods.description: Cancels all scheduled events in this scheduler and frees their callbacks. Returns the number of events that were removed.
methods.full_doc:
Cancels all scheduled events in this scheduler and frees their callbacks. Returns the number of events that were removed.
@return | integer | Count of events that were cancelled.
methods.return_description: Count of events that were cancelled.

methods.name: pause
methods.description: Pauses a scheduled event so it stops accumulating time. Returns true if the event was found and paused.
methods.params_doc: - `id` â€” `integer`: Event ID to pause.

methods.return_description: True if the named event exists and was paused.

methods.name: resumeNamed
methods.description: Resumes a previously paused named event. Returns true if the named event was found and resumed.
methods.params_doc: - `name` â€” `string`: The name used when scheduling.
methods.return_description: True if the named event exists and was resumed.

methods.name: isPausedNamed
methods.description: Checks whether a named scheduled event is currently paused.
methods.params_doc: - `name` â€” `string`: The name used when scheduling.
methods.return_description: True if the named event is paused.

methods.name: getRemaining
methods.description: Returns the remaining time in seconds before the event fires. The first return value indicates whether the event was found; the second is the remaining time (0.0 if not found).

methods.description: Returns the interval duration in seconds for a repeating event. The first return value indicates whether the event was found; the second is the interval (0.0 if not found).

methods.description: Returns the remaining repeat count for a repeating event. The first return value indicates whether the event was found; the second is the count (0 if not found). A value of -1 means infinite repeats.

methods.name: getCount

methods.full_doc:
Returns the total number of active scheduled events in this scheduler.
@return | integer | Count of active events.

methods.name: isEmpty

Returns true if the scheduler has no active events.
